title: FBX and Collada
sub: The pipeline workhorse and its open ancestor
cards/0/title: FBX: the workhorse of game dev
cards/0/body:
FBX started as the format of Kaydara’s Filmbox and has belonged to Autodesk since 2006. It stores meshes, materials, hierarchy, skeletons, animation, morphs, cameras and lights.

The format is closed. The official way to read it is the free but closed-source FBX SDK. Other programs rely on reverse engineering. Hence “an FBX from Blender looks wrong in Max”.
cards/1/title: Collada: open XML that never took off
cards/1/body:
DAE (Collada) was created at Sony Computer Entertainment, then moved to Khronos, the same group that makes glTF.

It is XML: human-readable, but heavy and too flexible, so every program understood it its own way. Today glTF has almost replaced it.
cards/2/q: Why does an FBX from one program sometimes open with errors in another?
cards/2/options/0: The format is closed, and not everyone uses the official SDK, so each program reads it a little differently
cards/2/options/2: Programs break other vendors’ files on purpose
cards/2/explain: No open spec means no guarantee that everyone reads the file the same way.
cards/3/q: An animator is moving a rigged character from Maya to Unity. What is used most often?
cards/3/explain: FBX is the de facto standard for moving animated models between DCC tools and engines.
cards/4/task: A scene with a skeleton and a camera from an old program. Try at least three formats and see where the skeleton gets lost.
cards/5/q: Which Collada line sets the units?
cards/5/explain: unit meter="1" means one file unit equals one meter.
cards/6/q: A Collada file says <up_axis>Z_UP</up_axis>. What will a Y-up viewer do?
cards/6/options/0: Rotate the model on import, if it reads the header correctly
cards/6/explain: The up axis is written in the file, so a good importer will rotate the model itself.
cards/7/q: What can FBX do? Select all.
cards/7/explain: It can do everything except be open.
